name: ISO6740FDWR
title: Quad-channel reinforced digital isolators, 50 Mbps, ISO6740, ISO6741, ISO6742
summary: Four-channel capacitive digital isolators in a 16-pin wide SOIC, rated 5000 VRMS for 60 s (UL 1577) and 1500 VRMS working voltage, carrying CMOS logic at up to 50 Mbps with 11 ns typical delay. Each side runs from 1.71 V to 1.89 V or 2.25 V to 5.5 V on its own, so the part also translates levels. ISO6740, ISO6741 and ISO6742 have 4, 3 and 2 forward channels; output enables set the outputs to high impedance, and on supply or input loss outputs go high, or low on the F versions such as ISO6740F.

circuits.title: Isolated SPI for an analog input module with 16 inputs
circuits.description: An MSP430G2132 talks SPI to an ADS7953 16-channel ADC across an ISO6741. Three lines go from the MCU to the ADC (P1.4 as chip select, SCLK, and MCU SDO into ADC SDI) on channels A to C; the ADC's SDO comes back on the reverse channel D. Power for the far side comes from the same 3.3 V rail: an SN6501 drives a centre-tapped 1:1.33 transformer, two MBR0520L Schottky diodes rectify the secondary, and a TLV70733 LDO makes the 3.3 V isolated rail (3.3 VISO). That rail supplies VCC2, the ADC's digital and analog supplies, and a REF5025 whose 2.5 V output is the ADC reference. Each enable pin is pulled up to its own side's supply through 4.7 kΩ, and each supply pin carries 0.1 µF. The ADC's 16 analog inputs are CH0 to CH15.
notes: U1 pins: VCC1 1, GND1 2 and 8, INA 3, INB 4, INC 5, OUTD 6, EN1 7, GND2 9 and 15, EN2 10, IND 11, OUTC 12, OUTB 13, OUTA 14, VCC2 16.
ADS7953 pins used: AGND 1 and 22, MXO 2, AINP 3, CH15 5, CH0 20, CS 23, SCLK 24, SDI 25, SDO 26, BDGND 27, VBD 28, REFM 30, REFP 31, VA 32.
SN6501: Vcc 2, D2 3, D1 1, GND 4 and 5. TLV70733: IN 4, EN 3, OUT 1, GND 2. REF5025: VIN 2, VOUT 6, GND 4.

circuits.title: Typical ISO674x circuit hook-up
circuits.description: The minimum circuit for an ISO6741: a 0.1 µF capacitor from VCC1 to GND1 and another from VCC2 to GND2, each within 2 mm of its supply pin. EN1 is tied to VCC1 and EN2 to VCC2, so all outputs stay active. INA, INB and INC enter on side 1 and leave as OUTA, OUTB, OUTC on side 2; IND enters on side 2 and leaves as OUTD on side 1. Both GND1 pins are joined, as are both GND2 pins.
notes: GND1 is pins 2 and 8; GND2 is pins 9 and 15.

circuits.title: Switching characteristics test circuit

Delays are timed between the 50 % points of input and output; rise and fall between 10 % and 90 % of the output swing.

circuits.title: Enable/disable propagation delay test circuit, input 0 V

The output has a 1 kΩ ±1 % load to the output supply and 15 pF (fixture included). Times run from the enable edge at VCC/2 to the output reaching 50 % of its swing, or moving 0.5 V from its level when it goes to high impedance.

operation.text: Three quad-channel reinforced digital isolators in one 16-pin wide SOIC: ISO6740 has all four channels running from side 1 to side 2, ISO6741 has three forward and one reverse, ISO6742 two each way. The F versions differ only in default output state: low instead of high.

Each channel uses on-off keying. The transmitter puts a high-frequency carrier across a capacitive SiO2 barrier for one logic state and nothing for the other; the receiver conditions the signal, detects its envelope and drives the output buffer. An oscillator and emissions-reduction circuitry sit on the transmit side. The barrier is a double capacitive silicon dioxide insulation.

EN1 controls the outputs on side 1 (ISO6741 and ISO6742 only) and EN2 the outputs on side 2. High or unconnected leaves the outputs active; low turns them to high impedance, which allows several masters on one line. ISO6740 has no EN1; its pin 7 is not connected. The enable input has an internal 550 kΩ pull-up to its side's supply.

With an open input, or with the input-side supply off, the output takes the default level: high on ISO674x, low on ISO674xF. When VCCI returns, outputs follow their inputs again. tDO, the delay to the default level after the input supply is lost, is 0.1 µs typical and 0.3 µs maximum, timed from VCC falling below 1.2 V.

Each side has its own UVLO: about 1.53 V rising (1.71 V maximum) and 1.41 V falling (1.1 V minimum), with 0.08 V minimum hysteresis. Valid data appears at most 300 µs after UVLO is cleared. The supported supply windows are 1.71 V to 1.89 V and 2.25 V to 5.5 V; between 1.89 V and 2.25 V, and between 1.05 V and 1.71 V, outputs are undetermined. With the output side unpowered the output is undetermined.

VCC1 and VCC2 are set independently anywhere in the supported range, so the part also shifts logic levels, for instance 3.3 V on side 1 and 5 V on side 2. Inputs and outputs are single-ended CMOS; the part follows no interface standard and is meant for CMOS or TTL single-ended lines, usually sitting between a microcontroller or FPGA and an ADC, DAC or line transceiver.

Each logic input has clamp diodes to VCCI and ground on both sides of a 985 Ω series resistor, then a 1.5 MΩ resistor: a pull-up to VCCI on parts without F, a pull-down to ground on F parts. The enable input has the same clamps and 985 Ω, then 20 kΩ in series and the 550 kΩ pull-up. Each output is a CMOS stage with about 20 Ω in series and clamp diodes to VCCO and ground.

operation.topic: Unpowered side fed from an input
operation.text: A hard-driven input whose own supply is floating can raise that supply a little through an internal protection diode; the output is then undetermined.

Inside the chip: strong ESD cells on the signal pins and on the bond pads between dies, tied to supply and ground through low resistance; isolation capacitors built to take ESD, EFT and surge; large on-chip decoupling; guard rings between PMOS and NMOS devices against parasitic SCR latch-up; and fully differential internal signalling to cut common-mode current across the barrier.
Only two parts are needed: 0.1 µF from VCC1 to GND1 and 0.1 µF from VCC2 to GND2, each placed no more than 2 mm from its supply pin. No bias or current-limit parts are needed, unlike an optocoupler.
When only one supply exists, the isolated side can be powered through a transformer driver such as the SN6501 or SN6505B. The 0.1 µF bypass capacitors go as close to VCC1 and VCC2 as they can.

Lifetime is projected by time-dependent dielectric breakdown testing: both sides shorted into a two-terminal device, high 60 Hz voltage applied across it over temperature, with the test in a 150 °C oven and a failure counted at more than 1 mA. VDE reinforced certification uses the TDDB line for under 1 ppm failure and adds 20 % on working voltage and 50 % on lifetime, so the barrier must last at least 30 years at 1.2 times the working voltage (20 years expected minimum at the working voltage). The TDDB data give 1500 VRMS for 36 years; the DW-16 working voltage is rated to 1500 VRMS, and lifetime is longer at lower voltages.

Two layers are the minimum for a low-cost, low-EMI board; four layers improve EMI. Four-layer order, top to bottom: high-speed signals, ground plane, power plane, low-speed signals. High-speed traces on top need no vias; the ground plane under them gives controlled impedance and a low-inductance return; ground and power planes next to each other add roughly 100 pF/inch² of bypass capacitance; slow control lines on the bottom tolerate vias. Extra layers are added as a second power/ground pair to keep the stack symmetric and flat.

Solid supply copper on each side carries the high peak currents into the VCC pins with low inductance; solid ground copper spreads heat. Keep the area under the part between the two sides free of planes, traces, pads and vias. The example stack is FR-4 (εr about 4.5) with 10 mil between the signal layers and their planes and 40 mil between the planes.

Standard FR-4 UL94V-0 suits digital boards below 150 Mbps (edges slower than 1 ns) with traces up to 10 inches: lower high-frequency loss and moisture uptake than cheaper laminates, stiffer and stronger, and self-extinguishing.

Two example land patterns for DW0016B: IPC-7351 nominal, pads 2 × 0.6 mm on 1.27 mm pitch with (9.3) mm between pad-row centres, giving 7.3 mm clearance and creepage; and an HV/isolation option with 1.65 × 0.6 mm pads and (9.75) mm row spacing, giving 8.1 mm. Non-solder-mask-defined pads have 0.07 mm maximum mask clearance all round; solder-mask-defined pads 0.07 mm minimum. The stencil example matches both patterns at 0.125 mm thickness.
